headline: The bulletin board got a life
lede: PAPERS, PLEASE-MIN's wanted sheet used to repeat itself — the same fake names drifted back onto the wall days apart, sometimes twice on one bulletin, and a wall name could walk up the window the next day as an innocent lookalike. The wall now prints a per-week plan: twenty distinct decoys, verified collision-free for every seed, and no row ever names a person standing in that week's line.

notes.text: Name pool doubled (80 to 192 combos) and decoy names moved from random draws to an index walk the harness proves distinct analytically, on the sweep, and live in the browser.
Readability: five 9px rows sit at the fit-law ceiling (2 px of slack), so the fix was contrast — the wanted rows print in a brighter red that holds at arm's length on a phone.
Balance recorded honestly: half-name near-misses stay by design — the printed law is NAME *AND* NUMBER, and the wanted trap exists to teach exactly that discrimination.
All 43 mutants die (two new: frozen day-term, unseeded plan); papersplay now matches the browser's whole week of bulletin rows against Node's plan row-for-row, name and number.
